title: Multimodal ECoG Speech Neuroprosthesis With Voice Synthesis & Facial Avatar
aiSystem: Multimodal RNN + CTC + HuBERT Speech & Avatar Decoder
whyItMatters: First brain–computer interface to simultaneously decode text at 78 words per minute, synthesize a personalized voice, and animate a real-time expressive facial avatar from brain surface signals.
summary: Sean Metzger, Kaylo Littlejohn, Gopala Anumanchipalli, Edward Chang, and colleagues (UCSF & UC Berkeley) demonstrated in Nature (August 2023, published alongside Stanford’s intracortical speech BCI) a high-density 253-channel surface electrocorticography (ECoG) neuroprosthesis in a woman with severe paralysis from brainstem stroke. Using deep recurrent neural networks paired with CTC phoneme decoding, self-supervised speech-unit synthesis (HuBERT), and facial-blendshape regression, the system decoded 1,024-word vocabulary sentences at a median 78 words per minute (4.9% WER on 50-phrase sets, 25.5% on 1,024 words) while driving both a voice cloned from her pre-injury wedding video and a real-time digital avatar displaying speech articulation and emotional expressions.
technicalHighlights: Decoded continuous attempted speech at 78 words per minute (approaching conversational speed) from non-penetrating 253-channel surface ECoG electrodes.
First BCI to unify three communication modalities—real-time text, personalized acoustic speech synthesis, and expressive facial-avatar animation.
Phoneme-level deep decoding generalized to a 39,000+ word vocabulary and rapidly decoded non-speech facial expressions (happy, sad, surprised).
caveats: Demonstrated in a single clinical trial participant using a wired transcutaneous pedestal; wireless fully implantable hardware and lower open-vocabulary error rates remain active engineering goals.

scoreRationale.foundational: Pioneered multimodal neural decoding unifying phonemes, personalized voice synthesis, and embodied facial articulation from ECoG.
scoreRationale.ripple: Set the clinical benchmark for expressive, human-centered speech neuroprosthetics restoring voice identity and nonverbal cues.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (Aug 2023) with full open clinical benchmarks in a brainstem-stroke participant.
scoreRationale.velocity: Pushed surface-ECoG speech decoding from ~15 WPM to 78 WPM with simultaneous avatar animation.

sources.label: Nature (2023): A high-performance neuroprosthesis for speech decoding and avatar control
